```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(CanadaForestAllometry)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

DBH–height (`hd_*()`) models predict **total tree height (m)** from diameter at
breast height (DBH, cm, measured at 1.3 m). They are typically used to fill in
heights of trees that were not measured, before applying a volume or biomass
model that requires height.

Many published DBH–height models need more than DBH: stand-level predictors
such as basal area, stems per hectare or dominant height, climate normals, or
ecological classification codes. Each source also defines these predictors
differently (size thresholds, all-species vs species-specific totals,
dominant-height definitions). For this reason:

- each model is a separate function whose arguments are exactly the
  predictors that model uses;
- you choose the model, and a missing required predictor is an error, never
  replaced by a proxy;
- a registry and two helper functions let you find which models suit your
  data, and what each predictor means in the source publication;
- for convenience, `hd()` selects a model automatically per tree (like
  `vol()`); see [Automatic model selection](#hd-auto).

# DBH–height models included in the package

```{r}
#| label: hd-model-list
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
reg <- CanadaForestAllometry:::hd_model_registry_species()

fmt_args <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) "—" else paste0("`", x, "`", collapse = ", ")
}

reg_fun <- reg |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$engine) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    reference = dplyr::first(.data$reference),
    province_scope = paste(sort(unique(unlist(.data$province_scope))), collapse = ", "),
    stand_origin = {
      o <- unique(.data$stand_origin)
      if (length(o) == 1L) o else "both"
    },
    variants = paste0("`", .data$model_id, "`", collapse = ", "),
    n_species = max(.data$n_species),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

origin_text <- c(
  natural = "natural stands",
  plantation = "plantations",
  both = "natural stands and plantations"
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(reg_fun))) {
  x <- reg_fun[i, ]
  cat(
    "- [`", x$engine, "()`](../reference/", x$engine, ".html) [", x$reference, "]. ",
    "Coverage: ", x$province_scope, ", ", origin_text[[x$stand_origin]], ". ",
    x$n_species, " species. Model ID(s): ", x$variants, ".\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

# Finding a model for your data

`find_hd_models()` filters the registry by jurisdiction and species, and
reports which required predictors each candidate lacks. Models with missing
predictors are kept as "near misses", so you can see what extra data would
make them usable:

```{r}
find_hd_models(
  jurisdiction = "ON",
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  available = c("DBH", "BA", "TPH")
) |>
  dplyr::select(model_id, usable, missing_predictors)
```

`hd_model_registry()` returns the full metadata table, and
`get_hd_model_info()` returns one model's species coverage and the source
definition of each predictor:

```{r}
get_hd_model_info("sharmaparton2007")$predictors
```

# Predictors

Predictor arguments follow a shared vocabulary (upper-case acronyms,
lower-case words). The exact definition of each quantity (size threshold,
species basis, dominant-height definition) is **model-specific**: see the
function's help page or `get_hd_model_info()`.

| Argument | Level | Units | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DBH` | tree | cm | Diameter at breast height (1.3 m) |
| `species` | tree | NFI code | Species code, e.g. `PICE.MAR` |
| `BA` | plot | m²/ha | Stand basal area |
| `TPH` | plot | stems/ha | Stand density |
| `HDOM` | plot | m | Dominant (or dominant and codominant) height |
| `HTOP` | plot | m | Top height: mean height of the largest-DBH trees (e.g. 100/ha) |
| `QMD` | plot | cm | Quadratic mean DBH |
| `DMEAN` | plot | cm | Arithmetic mean DBH |
| `DDOM` | plot | cm | Mean DBH of the dominant trees |
| `DMAX` | plot | cm | Maximum DBH in the plot |
| `BAL` | tree | m²/ha | Basal area of trees larger than the subject tree |
| `CCF` | plot | % | Crown competition factor |
| `CSI` | plot | m | Climate-derived site index (Acadian Region) |
| `MAT` | plot | °C | Mean annual temperature |
| `MAP` | plot | mm | Mean (total) annual precipitation |
| `elevation` | plot | m | Elevation above sea level |
| region / classification | plot | code | Model-specific descriptive names, e.g. `natural_subregion` (AB), `bioclim_subdomain`, `physical_env`, `potential_veg` (QC) |

Plot-level predictors can be given as a single value (recycled to all trees)
or one value per tree. The package does not compute stand variables from tree
lists: compute `BA`, `TPH`, `HDOM`, etc. following the definition of the model
you use.

# Using the models

All `hd_*()` functions are vectorized, return a tibble with a `height` column
(m), and can be used directly inside `dplyr::mutate()`:

```{r}
#| message: false
trees <- tibble::tibble(
  plot = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18, 30, 9),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "PINU.BAN", "POPU.TRE", "PICE.GLA", "ABIE.BAL"),
  HDOM = c(16, 16, 16, 22, 22),
  BA = c(30, 30, 30, 18, 18),
  TPH = c(3000, 3000, 3000, 1200, 1200)
)

trees |>
  dplyr::mutate(hd_sharmaparton2007(DBH, species, HDOM = HDOM, BA = BA, TPH = TPH))
```

When a source defines several model variants, the variant is chosen from the
inputs you supply (e.g. `hd_eslamdoust2026()` uses M5 only when `HDOM`, `BA`
and `TPH` are all given), or explicitly through `variant` when variants need
different inputs. Set `keep_model_id = TRUE` to return the variant used:

```{r}
hd_eslamdoust2026(
  DBH = c(15, 30),
  species = c("ACER.SAH", "PINU.STR"),
  HDOM = 22, BA = 30, TPH = 1200,
  keep_model_id = TRUE
)
```

Rows with `NA` in a required input return `NA` height. Inputs outside the
range of the source's fitting data are still computed, with a warning.

The functions return **population-level** predictions (random effects set to
zero). Calibrating a model to a plot with measured heights is not implemented
yet; the `calibration_published` column of `hd_model_registry()` shows which
sources publish the variance components needed for it.

# Automatic model selection with `hd()` {#hd-auto}

`hd()` is the DBH–height counterpart of `vol()`: it selects a model for each
tree from the registry and returns its height prediction. Supply whatever
predictors you have as named arguments, using the `hd_*()` argument names:

```{r}
trees <- tibble::tibble(
  DBH = c(15, 22, 30, 25, 18, 30),
  species = c("PINU.BAN", "PICE.MAR", "PICE.GLA", "ACER.SAH", "PICE.MAR", "PSEU.MEN"),
  jurisdiction = c("ON", "ON", "AB", "ON", "QC", "BC"),
  stand_origin = c("natural", "natural", "natural", "natural", "plantation", "natural"),
  HDOM = c(NA, 18, NA, NA, 12, NA),
  DDOM = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 15, NA),
  BA = c(NA, 25, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  TPH = c(NA, 1500, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  natural_subregion = c(NA, NA, "CM", NA, NA, NA),
  bec_zone = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "CWH")
)

trees |>
  dplyr::mutate(hd(
    DBH, species, jurisdiction,
    HDOM = HDOM, DDOM = DDOM, BA = BA, TPH = TPH,
    natural_subregion = natural_subregion,
    bec_zone = bec_zone, stand_origin = stand_origin
  )) |>
  dplyr::select(species, jurisdiction, height, model_id)
```

For each tree, a model is **eligible** when:

1. its jurisdiction coverage includes the tree's `jurisdiction`;
2. it has coefficients for the tree's `species` (exact match; there is no
   genus-level fallback);
3. every required predictor is supplied and not `NA` for that tree (`NA`
   means "not available"), so different trees can use different models;
4. its stand origin is compatible (see below);
5. in British Columbia, its coastal/interior coverage matches the tree's
   (see below).

The eligible model with the highest `rank` in `hd_model_registry()` is used.
Optional predictors (e.g. `natural_subregion`) are passed on when not `NA`.
If a model fails for a tree (e.g. a species-specific predictor of
`hd_auger2016()` is missing, or a region code is not recognised), the
next-ranked model is tried. Trees with no eligible or successful model get
`NA` height with a warning; this includes jurisdictions with no DBH–height
model yet.

The ranking prefers, within a jurisdiction, models that use more stand
information, more recent models over the ones they supersede, and models
fitted to the tree's region and stand origin:

```{r}
#| label: hd-rank-table
#| echo: false
hd_model_registry() |>
  dplyr::select(model_id, rank, province_scope, stand_origin, bc_region,
                required_predictors) |>
  tidyr::unnest(province_scope) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    required_predictors = vapply(required_predictors, paste, "", collapse = ", ")
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(province_scope, dplyr::desc(rank)) |>
  dplyr::rename(jurisdiction = province_scope) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Stand origin

`stand_origin` (`"natural"`, the default, or `"plantation"`) controls which
models are eligible. Plantation-only models (e.g. `hd_auger2025()`) are used
only for plantation trees. For plantation trees, models fitted to plantations
or to both origins are preferred; if none is eligible, a natural-stand model
is used and `hd()` warns.

## British Columbia: coast and interior

Some BC models were fitted to only part of the province:
`hd_temesgen2004()` to the interior (IDF zone) and
`hd_staudhammerlemay2000()` to the coast (CWH zone). Give either `bec_zone`
or `bc_region` (`"coastal"` or `"interior"`) to restrict them to trees in
the matching region. `CWH`, `CDF`, `MH` and `CMA` are treated as coastal, and
all other current zones as interior. If neither is supplied, both remain
eligible and `hd()` warns when one is used:

```{r}
hd(
  DBH = c(30, 30), species = "PSEU.MEN", jurisdiction = "BC",
  bec_zone = c("CWH", "IDF")
)
```

## Comparing candidate models

Use `pick_best = FALSE` to run every eligible model. It returns one tibble
per tree, ordered from most to least preferred, which can be unnested to see
how sensitive predictions are to model choice:

```{r}
trees[2, ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(candidates = hd(
    DBH, species, jurisdiction, HDOM = HDOM, BA = BA, TPH = TPH,
    pick_best = FALSE
  )) |>
  tidyr::unnest(candidates) |>
  dplyr::select(species, jurisdiction, height, model_id)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`hd()` passes the same `BA`, `HDOM`, `TPH`, … values to every model, but
sources define these differently (e.g. all-species vs species-specific
basal area, minimum DBH thresholds, dominant vs top height). Check the
definitions of the selected model with `get_hd_model_info()`, and call the
`hd_*()` function directly when you need a specific model.
:::

# Model curves

The figures below show population-level DBH–height curves for each model and
species. For models with stand-level predictors, curves are shown for the
reference plot values stated with each figure; heights for other plots can
differ substantially. Some curves are limited to the fitting DBH range of each
species.

```{r}
#| label: hd-curve-helper
#| echo: false
plot_hd_curves <- function(data, colour = NULL, colour_lab = NULL, ncol = 4) {
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = .data$DBH, y = .data$height)
  )
  if (is.null(colour)) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.6)
  } else {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::geom_line(
        ggplot2::aes(colour = factor(.data[[colour]])),
        linewidth = 0.6
      ) +
      ggplot2::labs(colour = colour_lab)
  }
  p +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(.data$species), ncol = ncol) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "DBH (cm)", y = "Height (m)") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

hd_species <- function(model_id) get_hd_model_info(model_id)$species

fig_height <- function(n_species, ncol = 4) 1.0 + 2.0 * ceiling(n_species / ncol)
```

## `hd_huang1994()`

Alberta [@Huang1994hd]. Provincial models (no `natural_subregion`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-huang1994
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(length(hd_species("huang1994")))
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = hd_species("huang1994"), DBH = seq(1, 60, by = 1))
grid$height <- hd_huang1994(grid$DBH, grid$species)$height
plot_hd_curves(grid)
```


## `hd_sharma2016()`

Ontario [@Sharma2016]. `HDOM` = 16 m, `BA` = 25 m²/ha, `TPH` = 2,200 stems/ha.

```{r}

```

## `hd_sharmazhang2004()`

Northern Ontario [@SharmaZhang2004]. Eq. 2 with `TPH` = 1,500 stems/ha and several `BA` values; eq. 5 (DBH only).

```{r}
#| label: fig-sharmazhang2004
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(length(hd_species("sharmazhang2004_eq2"))) + 0.5
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  species = hd_species("sharmazhang2004_eq2"),
  BA = c(12.5, 25, 37.5, 50),
  DBH = seq(1, 45, by = 1)
)
grid$height <- hd_sharmazhang2004(
  grid$DBH, grid$species, BA = grid$BA, TPH = 1500
)$height
eq5 <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  species = hd_species("sharmazhang2004_eq5"),
  BA = "eq. 5 (DBH only)",
  DBH = seq(1, 45, by = 1)
)
eq5$height <- hd_sharmazhang2004(eq5$DBH, eq5$species, variant = "eq5")$height
grid$BA <- paste0("eq. 2, BA = ", grid$BA)
plot_hd_curves(dplyr::bind_rows(grid, eq5), colour = "BA", colour_lab = "Model")
```

## `hd_huang2009()`

Alberta black spruce [@Huang2009hd]. Model 9 (DBH only), 10 (`HTOP` = 16 m) and 11 (`HTOP` = 16 m, `BA` = 15 m²/ha).

```{r}
#| label: fig-huang2009

#| warning: false

plot_hd_curves(grid, colour = "model", colour_lab = "Model")
```

## `hd_temesgen2004()`

Interior British Columbia [@Temesgen2004]. Model 2 (DBH only) and Model 7 with `BA` = 25 m²/ha, `TPH` = 800 stems/ha, `BAL` = 10 m²/ha.

```{r}
#| label: fig-temesgen2004
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(8) + 0.5
dbh_max <- CanadaForestAllometry:::get_params_tbl("parameters_hd_Temesgen2004") |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variant == "m2", !.data$Species %in% c("PICE.GLA", "PICE.ENG.GLA")) |>
  dplyr::select("Species", "DBH_max")
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = dbh_max$Species, DBH = seq(2, 105, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dbh_max, by = c(species = "Species")) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$DBH <= .data$DBH_max)
m2 <- dplyr::mutate(grid, model = "2", height = hd_temesgen2004(DBH, species)$height)
m7 <- dplyr::mutate(
  grid,
  model = "7",
  height = hd_temesgen2004(DBH, species, BAL = 10, TPH = 800, BA = 25)$height
)
plot_hd_curves(dplyr::bind_rows(m2, m7), colour = "model", colour_lab = "Model")
```

## `hd_staudhammerlemay2000()`

Coastal British Columbia [@StaudhammerLeMay2000]. Variant `"dbh"` (one curve per species) and variant `"density"` for three stands (A, B and C). For the conifers (eq 2b), stands A–C have `DMAX` = 40, 70 and 100 cm and each curve runs from 10 % of `DMAX` up to `DMAX`. For red alder (eq 2a), stands A–C have `TPH` = 1,000, 3,371 and 6,000 stems/ha and `BA` = 15, 30.7 and 50 m²/ha.

Eq 2b predicts height from relative DBH (`DBH / DMAX`). Within a stand, small trees are suppressed, and the curve drops slightly for the largest trees, past about 0.85–0.95 of `DMAX`. This drop comes from the published coefficients.

```{r}
#| label: fig-staudhammerlemay2000
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(4) + 0.5
dbh_max <- CanadaForestAllometry:::get_params_tbl("parameters_hd_StaudhammerLeMay2000") |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variant == "dbh") |>
  dplyr::select("Species", "DBH_max")
v_dbh <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = dbh_max$Species, DBH = seq(2, 100, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dbh_max, by = c(species = "Species")) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$DBH <= .data$DBH_max) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    curve = "dbh",
    height = hd_staudhammerlemay2000(DBH, species)$height
  )
stands <- tibble::tibble(
  stand = c("A", "B", "C"),
  DMAX = c(40, 70, 100),
  TPH = c(1000, 3371, 6000),
  BA = c(15, 30.73, 50)
)
v_conif <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  species = setdiff(dbh_max$Species, "ALNU.RUB"),
  stands,
  DBH = seq(2, 100, by = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$DBH >= 0.1 * .data$DMAX, .data$DBH <= .data$DMAX) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    curve = paste("density, stand", stand),
    height = hd_staudhammerlemay2000(DBH, species, variant = "density", DMAX = DMAX)$height
  )
v_alder <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  species = "ALNU.RUB",
  stands,
  DBH = seq(2, dbh_max$DBH_max[dbh_max$Species == "ALNU.RUB"], by = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    curve = paste("density, stand", stand),
    height = hd_staudhammerlemay2000(
      DBH, species, variant = "density", TPH = TPH, BA = BA
    )$height
  )
plot_hd_curves(dplyr::bind_rows(v_dbh, v_conif, v_alder), colour = "curve", colour_lab = NULL)
```

## `hd_rijal2012()`

Acadian Region [@Rijal2012]. GNLS and NLME coefficients with `BAL` = 10 m²/ha, `CCF` = 150, `CSI` = 15 m.

```{r}
#| label: fig-rijal2012
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(15, ncol = 5)
dbh_rng <- CanadaForestAllometry:::get_params_tbl("parameters_hd_Rijal2012") |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variant == "gnls") |>
  dplyr::select("Species", "DBH_min", "DBH_max")
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = dbh_rng$Species, DBH = seq(1, 56, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dbh_rng, by = c(species = "Species")) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$DBH >= .data$DBH_min, .data$DBH <= .data$DBH_max)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("gnls", "nlme"), function(v) {
  dplyr::mutate(
    grid,
    variant = v,
    height = hd_rijal2012(DBH, species, CSI = 15, CCF = 150, BAL = 10, variant = v)$height
  )
}))
plot_hd_curves(curves, colour = "variant", colour_lab = "Variant", ncol = 5)
```

## `hd_auger2016()`

Québec [@Auger2016]. `BA` = 20 m²/ha, `QMD` = 20 cm, `bioclim_subdomain` = `"4est"`, `physical_env` = `"2"`, `potential_veg` = `"MS2"`, `MAT` = 2 °C, `MAP` = 1,000 mm, `elevation` = 300 m.

```{r}
#| label: fig-auger2016
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(length(hd_species("auger2016")), ncol = 5)
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = hd_species("auger2016"), DBH = seq(9, 60, by = 1))
grid$height <- hd_auger2016(
  grid$DBH, grid$species,
  BA = 20, QMD = 20, bioclim_subdomain = "4est", physical_env = "2", potential_veg = "MS2",
  MAT = 2, MAP = 1000, elevation = 300, disturbance = "none"
)$height
plot_hd_curves(grid, ncol = 5)
```

## `hd_fortin2009()`

Québec [@Fortin2009]; superseded by `hd_auger2016()`. `BA` = 20 m²/ha, `QMD` = 20 cm, `ecoregion` = `"4d"`, `drainage` = `"mesic"`, `MAT` = 2 °C.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fortin2009
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr fig_height(length(hd_species("fortin2009")), ncol = 5)
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = hd_species("fortin2009"), DBH = seq(9.1, 60, by = 1))
grid$height <- hd_fortin2009(
  grid$DBH, grid$species,
  BA = 20, QMD = 20, ecoregion = "4d", drainage = "mesic", MAT = 2,
  disturbance = "none"
)$height
plot_hd_curves(grid, ncol = 5)
```

## `hd_auger2025()`

Québec plantations [@Auger2025]. The dashed line is variant `"dbh"`, the population-average curve. It is a Korf curve with a very large asymptote, so it does not level off within the data range. The coloured lines are the plot-specific variants for three plots:

- `"plot_mean_dbh"`: `DMEAN` = 6, 12 and 18 cm.
- `"dominant"`: `HDOM` / `DDOM` = 6 m / 8 cm, 12 m / 16 cm and 18 m / 24 cm.

```{r}
#| label: fig-auger2025
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
dbh_max <- CanadaForestAllometry:::get_params_tbl("parameters_hd_Auger2025") |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variant == "dbh") |>
  dplyr::select("Species", "DBH_max")
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = dbh_max$Species, DBH = seq(0.5, 40, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dbh_max, by = c(species = "Species")) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$DBH <= .data$DBH_max)
v_dbh <- dplyr::mutate(grid, height = hd_auger2025(DBH, species)$height)
plots <- tibble::tibble(
  plot = c("low", "medium", "high"),
  DMEAN = c(6, 12, 18),
  HDOM = c(6, 12, 18),
  DDOM = c(8, 16, 24)
)
v_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(grid, plots) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      variant = "plot_mean_dbh",
      height = hd_auger2025(DBH, species, variant = "plot_mean_dbh", DMEAN = DMEAN)$height
    ),
  tidyr::expand_grid(grid, plots) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      variant = "dominant",
      height = hd_auger2025(
        DBH, species, variant = "dominant", HDOM = HDOM, DDOM = DDOM
      )$height
    )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    plot = factor(.data$plot, levels = plots$plot),
    variant = factor(.data$variant, levels = c("plot_mean_dbh", "dominant"))
  )
ggplot2::ggplot(v_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = .data$DBH, y = .data$height)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = tidyr::expand_grid(v_dbh, variant = unique(v_plot$variant)),
    linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(colour = .data$plot), linewidth = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    ggplot2::vars(.data$variant), ggplot2::vars(.data$species)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "DBH (cm)", y = "Height (m)", colour = "Plot") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
